rationale_code: Deprecated alias registered with `readTextFileHandler`, which calls `validatePath` then `readFileContent`/`tailFile`/`headFile` and returns raw local file contents to the agent. Any file under the allowed directories (user's own project/home data) is read with the user's credentials, so it returns n
Same `readTextFileHandler`: reads local file text via `fs.readFile` and returns it in the tool result — non-public host file content.
`readFileAsBase64Stream` streams any local file (mime default `application/octet-stream`, i.e. arbitrary binary) and returns it base64-encoded in the result, exposing non-public host file bytes.
Loops `validatePath` + `readFileContent` over caller-supplied paths and concatenates the contents into the result — bulk exfiltration of local file content into agent context.

`writeFileContent` writes agent-supplied text to a path constrained by `validatePath`/`isPathWithinAllowedDirectories` on the local filesystem. The destination is local and not attacker-readable, so it is not a SINK; it returns only a success string, so no SECRET/UNTRUSTED. Not labelled HOSTEXEC bec

`applyFileEdits` reads the target file, applies agent-supplied replacements and writes atomically inside allowed directories. Output is a unified diff of a file the user already owns and the agent chose; local write is not an attacker-readable destination, so no SINK. The diff does echo file content
`fs.mkdir` with `recursive:true` on a `validatePath`-checked path; returns only a success message. No data return, no external destination, no execution.
`fs.readdir` returns the names of files/directories on the user's host, which is non-public local data returned into agent context.
`fs.readdir` plus `fs.stat` per entry returns local filenames and sizes — non-public host filesystem metadata.
`buildTree` recursively walks the allowed directory with `fs.readdir` and returns the full JSON name/type tree — non-public host filesystem structure.
Both paths pass `validatePath`; `moveFile` renames within allowed directories and returns only a success string. No data disclosure, no external destination, no execution.
`searchFilesWithValidation` recursively walks the local tree and returns full matching paths — non-public host filesystem information.
`getFileStats` returns size, timestamps, permissions and type of a local file — non-public host metadata.
Returns the absolute local paths of the configured roots (`allowedDirectories`), revealing usernames/home layout of the host — non-public local configuration data. No input, no write, no network.
